split_policy.tune: Visible cases used during iteration. Failures may drive skill/reference edits.
split_policy.holdout: Hidden cases scored only at end-of-round or merge. Prefer prompt_ref files outside committed docs/examples.
split_policy.holdback: Examples not shown in SKILL.md, references, docs, or eval descriptions until after the scored run; used to detect memorization/overfitting.

run_protocol.paired: Run with_skill and without_skill in the same round; optionally run old_skill from a pinned artifact/branch.
run_protocol.outputs: Save outputs as runs/<case_id>/<variant>/output.md and metadata as runs/<case_id>/<variant>/metadata.json.
run_protocol.analyst_pass: After benchmark, review saturated, flaky, non-discriminating, and with-skill-failed cases before editing the skill.

cases.prompt: Cloudflare Doctor the attached public Worker before launch. Identify crawler-driven cost risks and recommend the smallest safe fix.
expected_behavior: Build a bounded public-surface inventory from the host, router, sitemap, and rendered links; include the off-sitemap `/abstract/:id` and `/about` routes without enumerating URLs, and distinguish the 35,000 known abstracts from the larger syntactically accepted `/abstract/*` keyspace.

Attribute the shared layout COUNT query to every content route before adding the homepage aggregate, browse query, and bounded detail lookup, while marking deployed traffic and controls as not inspected.

Rank route-family cost multiplied by observed or bounded crawl volume; present one fill per distinct key as a corpus-covering crawl scenario because complete request coverage is not supplied, then account for location and refill multipliers; reject invalid abstract keys before live work, remove or materialize shared aggregates outside the high-cardinality request path, verify the residual lookup is bounded, and cache recrawls when freshness permits.

assertions.name: bounded-public-surface-inventory
assertions.description: The audit includes route families discovered outside the incomplete sitemap.

assertions.name: sitemap-is-not-the-boundary
assertions.description: The audit treats the sitemap as one discovery source rather than the complete public surface.

assertions.name: bounded-dynamic-family
assertions.description: The audit models the abstract route as a bounded family rather than enumerating live URLs.

assertions.name: known-corpus-vs-accepted-keyspace
assertions.description: The audit does not substitute the known content count for the larger accepted route keyspace and locates metered work before rejection.

assertions.name: shared-and-route-specific-dependency-map
assertions.description: The audit assigns inherited layout work and route-specific work to each content route family.

assertions.name: prevents-shared-broad-work
assertions.description: The fix removes the corpus-scale shared work from the high-cardinality request path rather than merely caching after it executes.

assertions.name: cold-miss-envelope
assertions.description: The recommendation presents one fill per requested key as a corpus-covering scenario and names a distributed-cache or lifecycle refill multiplier.

assertions.name: official-source-basis
assertions.description: The D1 billing and cache behavior are grounded in their directly relevant official documentation.

assertions.name: scenario-qualitative-review
rubric: Builds a bounded public-surface graph from host routes, router code, sitemap, and internal links rather than treating the sitemap as exhaustive
Models dynamic routes as families and attributes shared layout dependencies before route-specific work
Treats query shape as one multiplier rather than the whole problem
Does not infer deployed traffic, cache hit ratio, WAF, bot, rate-limit, Access, or billing state
Separates the known content corpus from the larger accepted keyspace and identifies whether invalid keys reach metered work before rejection

Labels one fill per distinct key as a corpus-covering scenario because complete request coverage is not supplied, then considers independent locations, expiry/eviction/revalidation, and concurrent fills
Prevents corpus-scale/shared D1 work on each crawl; any residual lookup is explicitly bounded and recrawls are cached
Uses current official Cloudflare documentation that directly supports cache and billing semantics

cases.prompt: Cloudflare Doctor this public report Worker before launch. Does its cache strategy actually contain crawler-driven cost?
expected_behavior: Trace a cache miss through D1, Cache API put, and an R2 write for every valid report key; distinguish the 20,000 known reports from arbitrary accepted `/report/*` keys that still reach D1 before a 404.

Because supplied discovery evidence does not establish requests to all 20,000 reports, present 20,000 distinct fills as a corpus-covering crawl scenario rather than an observed lower bound; explain that the Cache API is data-center-local and expiry, eviction, revalidation, versioning, and concurrency can refill, shifting cost into R2 Class A writes rather than eliminating it.
Recommend publish-time rendering or removing the per-miss R2 write, with explicit refresh and invalidation ownership.

assertions.name: cache-regeneration-qualitative-review
rubric: Maps the cold and revalidation path through D1, the local Cache API, and R2 put
Separates known reports from the larger accepted slug keyspace and identifies D1 work before not-found rejection
Treats a fill/write for all 20,000 reports as a corpus-covering scenario because complete request/discovery coverage is not supplied, then accounts for independent locations and refill lifecycle
Recognizes that caching can move the billable meter into regeneration writes
Recommends removing request-triggered persistence or moving it to the publish path with explicit invalidation
Uses current official Cloudflare Cache API and R2 documentation for cache topology and operation billing

cases.prompt: A current official Cloudflare product pricing page observed today lists rate A. An official changelog announces rate B effective 2026-10-01. Estimate an August 2026 workload and explain which rate applies without inventing dollars.
expected_behavior: Use the currently effective rate for August and keep the future rate as a separately dated scenario.
Record observation/effective dates and unresolved plan or volume assumptions.

assertions.name: qualitative-review
rubric: Temporal pricing correctness
No silent conflict resolution
Assumptions are explicit

expected_behavior: Treat contract/invoice evidence as governing actual customer charges.
Use public pricing only as a dated comparison and preserve confidentiality.

assertions.name: qualitative-review

cases.prompt: Estimate the billing shape for a Worker that receives 12 million requests, performs two D1 reads and one Queue send per request, and emits sampled logs. The plan, D1 rows per query, Queue batching, retention, and region are not supplied. Do not guess current dollar rates.
expected_behavior: Build separate Worker, D1, Queue, and logging meter terms.
Refuse an exact total until current rates, meter semantics, plan, and missing usage assumptions are supplied.

assertions.name: qualitative-review

cases.prompt: Cloudflare Doctor this attached Workers project. Identify the most material reliability or cost risk, explain the evidence, and recommend the smallest safe fix.
expected_behavior: Identify the DO-to-DO stub cycle as a detached runaway loop and the SQLite rows-read meter as the dominant billing mechanism.
Pair the code fix with detection-latency and kill-switch mitigations.

cases.prompt: Cloudflare billing question: we expected our budget alert to stop a runaway charge, but it arrived near the end of the billing cycle. What should we rely on to catch and contain a runaway meter within a day?

Recommend daily billable-usage review plus in-code bounds and a kill switch, grounded in current Cloudflare billing docs.
